Verse Home: a brochure plan to a home buyers walk, restyle and tour together#

You have the floor plan from a project brochure. A minute later you have a furnished home that walks like a real one. It opens on any phone from a WhatsApp link, changes style while people watch, and a group of buyers can tour it together from one link.

Verse Home combines three features: Floor plan to 3D home, Restyle a space, live and Tour together, live.

The flow#

  1. Upload the plan. Open the upload screen, choose Floor plan → 3D and drop the plan as a PNG, JPG, WebP or PDF. The plan can be a clean export, a tinted brochure page or a phone scan. Add the carpet area and the BHK if you know them. Both make the scale and the room types more reliable.
  2. Check the plan, then Generate. The plan comes back as a drawing. Tap a room to rename it or change its type, and rotate or flip the plan if needed. Doors we added because the plan didn't show them are highlighted in orange ("We added 2 doors — check them"). To change doors, press Edit doors and tap a wall to add a 0.9 m door there. Tap any door, window or open gap to switch it between the three, remove it or make it the entrance. Tap the green IN marker, then a door or an outside wall, to move the entrance. The line above the plan re-checks after every change and names any room that cannot be reached from the entrance. Add doors for me puts in the fewest doors that connect them. A room that still cannot be reached is not published.
  3. Share. The result shows the link, Copy and **Share on WhatsApp**. The link opens walking at the living-room entrance, with a pin for each room.
  4. Restyle. Anyone who opens the link can use the Restyle chip (Original, Scandinavian, Japandi, Luxury Marble, Indian Contemporary, Industrial, Coastal, or plain words such as marble floor). The floors, walls, ceilings, skirting, counters, joinery and fabrics change in place.
  5. Tour together. Tap Tour together on the link and send the invite. Buyers follow your camera from their phones, and when you restyle, everyone in the tour sees the change.

What a generated home is made of#

  • The shell. Walls are 3 m high with real door and window openings. Doors have architraves and panelled leaves and are drawn open. A single leaf hangs on the jamb nearer the room's corner, so it opens back against the side wall. A WC-sized bathroom's door opens out. Windows have frames, glass, a stone sill and architraves. Living and dining rooms get a false-ceiling border with a warm LED cove. Other rooms get a slim cornice, and every room has recessed downlights and its own floor, ceiling and skirting.
  • Furniture, placed the way a stylist would. In the living room the sofa sits on the longest solid wall with a rug under its front legs, a coffee table centred on the rug, a side table and lamp at one end and a floor lamp at the other. The TV unit faces the sofa on a slatted-wood or stone feature wall, with the TV mounted above it. Dining tables are centred under a pendant. Beds go against the longest wall without a window, with nightstands and lamps on both sides, a rug, and art at eye height above the headboard. Each bedroom has a wardrobe, and corners get plants and lounge chairs. Kitchens get a counter run with a sink and tap, a hob, a chimney hood, wall cabinets (never over a window), a backsplash and a fridge. Bathrooms get a WC, a vanity with a lit mirror and a shower. A glass enclosure (0.75–0.9 m) goes in where it fits. In a small WC the shower is a wet-room one: a rain head, a mixer and a floor drain on the open floor. A door that swings out of a small bathroom keeps only a 0.55 m approach inside it, not a full swing square. Living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms and studies get curtains. The rules stay as before: door-swing keep-outs, 0.75 m walkways, no overlaps and every room reachable on foot. The premium checks add two more: nothing floats, and every wall piece hangs on a wall.
  • Light. The generator bakes the light into the vertex colours with real rays (plan2home-bake.mjs, makeRayBaker): 40 cosine-weighted rays per vertex against the walls, furniture and floor and ceiling planes give soft contact shadows and ambient occlusion (corners, skirting, under a sofa, behind a bed). Rays that leave the flat through a window bring in daylight, and each room's lamps add warm pools. The occluder for a pack model is the model as drawn, not its furniture slot, and the shadow never goes below half brightness. A phone and a desktop render the same light without real-time GI, so the link opens with the studio fill (gi=0;env=1.25;ev=0.35). The bake takes 1–3 s of the build.
  • Surfaces. Floors, bathroom walls, counters, wood and the feature wall come from the shared CC0 material library (web/playground/assets/library), at world scale, with each set's own normal and roughness maps. Floors, wet walls, counters and joinery use the 1024² colour map, so they have at least 512 texture pixels per metre. The palettes are chosen per style (Modern Indian, Scandinavian, Luxury, Minimal).
  • Outside the windows. You see a city skyline: a horizon band cut from a CC0 Poly Haven panorama on a backdrop about 40 m outside the flat, with no lawn. It is far enough that it barely shifts as you walk past a window, and it fades into haze below the horizon instead of ending in a hard edge. Each style looks out at its own time of day and its own part of the skyline: golden hour for Modern Indian, a clear day for Scandinavian, blue hour for Luxury and an overcast sky for Minimal. The sky colour behind the windows matches. A build can name another time ("timeOfDay": "day" | "golden" | "dusk" | "overcast" in the /v1/plan2home/build body).
  • Room views, shot like an architectural photographer would. Each room's view (its pin, the tour stop and the hero still) is taken from a corner or just inside a doorway, at 1.3 m, with the camera level so walls stay vertical, looking across the room's longest diagonal. A view with an open door leaf in the frame is refused. Only a room with no leaf-free view at all falls back, first to a leaf at the frame's outer edge, then to one seen through a doorway 3 m or more away. So is a view that starts at a piece of furniture: a bedroom is shot across the room with the bed at three quarters, not from the foot of the bed. A WC-sized room is shot from its threshold or a step outside it, the way a photographer gains the distance the room lacks. Walking and the tour use a 26 mm lens (35 mm equivalent, measured on the diagonal, so a portrait phone gets the same lens) instead of the 55° vertical field of view, which was a 21 mm on a desktop and stretched the corners. A room view holds its 1.3 m height until you walk; walking rises to eye height. Where a photographer would use a shift lens, the view does too. Each view aims at its subject's height (about 0.85 m in a small bathroom, 0.9–1.0 m elsewhere). Through the walk lens the camera stays level and the frame slides down (up to 60 % of its half height), so a WC and basin a metre away are in the picture with the walls still vertical. The shift eases out as you walk and clears when you tilt the view. Pins follow the live lens and shift.
  • The furniture pack. Sofas, beds, wardrobes, kitchens, bathrooms, curtains and lamps are procedural, so they restyle. Armchairs and lounge chairs, coffee and side tables, the TV unit, dining chairs, plants, the pendant, vases, art, books and bowls are CC0 Poly Haven models from web/playground/assets/furniture (22 models, 6.1 MB). They are embedded once and instanced.
  • Every material follows the restyle naming contract (see Restyle). The soft goods, joinery and surfaces restyle. Hero models, art, plants, glass and lamps are never touched.

Where the furniture pack comes from (deploys)#

The pack is committed, so a deploy needs no network and no extra build step. web/playground is copied into the image as before, and .dockerignore only drops GLBs directly under assets/, not this sub-folder. It is deterministic: manifest.json holds each shipped file's sha256, and the generator checks it on load. A missing or altered file falls back to the procedural piece for that role and never fails a build. The size is capped at 12 MB by pack.mjs (6.1 MB today). To change it:

Code
node tools/plan2home-lib/fetch.mjs   # raw CC0 sources from polyhaven.com → ~/VerseTestAssets/plan2home-lib (local only)
node tools/plan2home-lib/pack.mjs    # Blender headless → web/playground/assets/furniture (commit the result)

The licence record is in docs/attributions.md.

Plan to Film: a 30-second film of the home#

Tap Film on any Verse Home (or Make a 30 s film on the build's done card, or Make a film after the home arrives on WhatsApp) and pick 9:16 (1080 × 1920, the default: for phones and stories) or 16:9 (1920 × 1080). The film is made in your browser from the home itself, and nothing is uploaded:

  1. your floor plan as a sheet on a softly lit desk, with a slow push-in (the picture you uploaded; a home built without one shows its plan drawing);
  2. the plan becomes glowing indigo lines, the walls rise from it, and the furnished home fades in under them, seen from above;
  3. the camera comes down over the entrance to eye height (1.5 m) and walks the home's walkthrough route, one short clip per room in route order, slowing for about a second in each room, with a quick cut from one room to the next (never a double exposure). Each room is shot from near the doorway it is entered by, looking at its furniture, at least 0.8 m from any piece and 0.5 m from the walls. The route is the scene's default camera path (the automatic walkthrough, or a path you drew on the plan), so the camera never passes through a wall;
  4. a cut to just above the last room, seen through the cutaway, and out into an aerial view of the whole home;
  5. an end card with the home's name, its link as text and as a QR code, and the Verse by Ctruh mark.

The film is 30 seconds at 30 fps: MP4 (H.264) where the browser can encode it, WebM elsewhere, about 15 MB at 1080 × 1920 so it fits a WhatsApp video. Every frame waits for the streamed textures to be in, so no frame is blurred, and the same home always gives the same film. A computer takes 1 to 3 minutes (measured on a recent laptop); a phone makes it at 720 × 1280. Cancel stops it at any time. Your plan sets the resolution and the mark, as for any video export.

The WhatsApp bot does not send the video itself: Make a film replies with the home's link with &film=1, which opens the film sheet on the phone, and Share sends the finished film on.

For scripting: await window.__versePlanFilm({ format: "9:16", download: false }) resolves the film (blob, width, height, frames, film.clips). The gate is web/test/fix-verify-planfilm.mjs.

Change the sofa, the floor, the walls (swaps)#

Tap Change in the viewer. The sheet lists what this home can swap, with two or three curated options each, all from the CC0 library:

CategoryOptions
SofaTan leather, Taupe weave, Ivory bouclé
Bed (headboard)Walnut panel, Charcoal leather, Ivory bouclé
Dining tableWalnut, White marble, Light oak
Flooring (dry rooms)White marble, Natural oak, Terrazzo
Wall paintWarm white, Soft greige, Sage green
CurtainsIvory linen, Taupe, Navy
RugCream wool, Navy wool, Terracotta
Kitchen counterBlack marble, White marble, Terrazzo

Tap a thumbnail to apply it, or tap something in the room while the sheet is open to jump to its category. Undo steps back. A choice rides in the link's ?style= (x.sofa=leather-tan), the same way a Restyle look does, so the link you share opens with it. The device also remembers the last look for each home, so a reload keeps it. A Restyle preset changes the room around the pieces you chose.

Say it. Press and hold the mic in the sheet (phone or desktop) and say "show me a leather sofa", "make the floor marble", "try a lighter wall colour", "change the bed", "undo" or "what other options are there?". You can also type it. The words go to Ask Verse, which calls its swap and swap_undo tools. Without an AI key, a built-in grammar (swaps.js) answers. The reply is shown and read out. Every spoken change also has a button to tap.

How fast#

In short: a floor plan becomes a shareable 3D home link in about 2 s of compute (1.4–1.7 s measured: the warm median on an M5 Pro over 8 repeats, CV reader, 16 Oct 2026; the first upload after a server start takes 2.3–5.9 s), and in about 15 s end to end with the AI reader.

These times were measured by web/test/fix-verify-instanthome.mjs on a laptop with no AI key (CV reader only), after the premium pass:

StepSynthetic PNG (2BHK)Scanned JPEG (3BHK)
Read the plan0.18 s0.36 s
Generate (furnish, bake, pack)0.31 s0.27 s
Compile + publish2.3 s1.9 s
Upload → link ready2.8 s2.5 s
  • Through the UI, from upload to the result: 3.6 s on a desktop and 4.1 s on an emulated iPhone 13.
  • With the AI reader, on real brochure plans and recorded Haiku 5.5 answers (web/test/instanthome-ai-e2e.mjs, with no key and no network), upload to link ready took 2.8–3.0 s. A live model adds its own latency on top (a median of about 12 s), so the real figure is about 15 s.
  • The gate fails if any of these is over 60 s.
  • Opening a link, the first picture arrives in about 0.5 s on a desktop and 1.2–2.2 s on a phone. The link settles in about 5–6 s.
  • Phone memory is 50–96 MB for a 1BHK to a 3BHK (the target is under 150 MB, the budget 256 MB).
  • Sizes: a home is a 7–11 MB GLB and a 13–20 MB .vpk, which streams. Before the premium pass the .vpk was 2–3 MB.

Limits#

  • A noisy scan can lose a door. The reader adds the most likely one and highlights it. A room that no door can legally reach (one with no shared wall, or one reached only through a bathroom) is named in the plan editor, and you fix it there before you generate. If a room marked Bathroom is really a passage, change its type and the repair works.
  • The light is baked into the vertex colours, so it does not change if you move a piece in an editor. The real-time GI stays off for generated homes.
  • Very small rooms (a 1.4 m toilet, a 2 × 2 m bedroom) get fewer pieces than the stylist minimum. The gate counts only rooms of 4 m² or more, and bedrooms under 7 m² need two pieces.
  • The view is one panorama graded to four times of day. It is a fixed picture, so it does not change while you watch, and its towers do not move against each other as you walk (they all sit at the same 40 m).
  • A WC cubicle under about 0.9 m wide with its door in a long wall has no room for a fixture outside the door's approach, so it stays empty.

Gate#

web/test/fix-verify-instanthome.mjs runs on a real GPU (WebGPU on the desktop, WebGL2 on an emulated iPhone 13). Without a GPU (a Linux container), run the WebGL2 tier on SwiftShader:

Code
cd web/test && QA_GPU=swiftshader QA_CHROME=/path/to/chrome QA_TIERS=c \
  QA_EXTRA_Q="&texfmt=0&watchdog=120000" QA_PORT=10520 node fix-verify-instanthome.mjs

texfmt=0 streams RGBA textures (BC7 crashes SwiftShader's GPU process), watchdog gives a slow software frame time before the viewer restarts its render worker, and stills are read back from the canvas. Tier A and the tier A/C parity checks are reported as not run. instanthome-premium.mjs takes the same variables (--q "&tier=c&texfmt=0&watchdog=120000", and QA_PHONE_DPR=2 to halve the phone's pixels).

The gate checks:

  • the naming contract on 24 generated homes;
  • upload → link ready ≤ 60 s for a synthetic PNG and a scanned JPEG, over HTTP and through the UI;
  • that the link opens walking at the spawn, is textured, and has the Restyle chip and Tour together;
  • that no room is dark;
  • phone memory ≤ 256 MB;
  • desktop vs phone mean ΔE76 ≤ 3;
  • that every Restyle preset changes the floors and the walls, and that Original restores the first frame;
  • a three-person tour, in which both guests follow the host and receive the host's restyle;
  • that no page shows an error;
  • the premium pass, across all six synthetic layouts:
    • furniture per room type (living room ≥ 5 pieces, bedroom ≥ 3, or 2 under 7 m², kitchen ≥ 2, bathroom ≥ 2);
    • zero overlaps, and nothing floating: pieces stand on the floor, props on their part's drawn top, wall pieces hang on a wall and pendants hang from the ceiling;
    • baked AO in every floor's vertex colours;
    • the furniture pack's models in use;
    • every room view within mean ΔE76 ≤ 3 between phone and desktop.

Screenshots go to web/test/out/instanthome/. The hero set (a 1BHK, a 2BHK and a 3BHK; living room, kitchen, master bedroom and bathroom on a desktop and an iPhone 13; a preset sheet) is made by web/test/instanthome-premium.mjs into web/test/out/instanthome/premium/. web/test/instanthome-ai-e2e.mjs times upload to link ready on real brochure plans, with the AI reader answering from recorded replays.
